What should happen: A new visitor can understand the service and find the next step.
The chosen service and what is included stay clear.
They answer the same customer question without conflicting promises.
Locations, examples, prices and exclusions match the real business.

What to check: Ask your web person about search settings
What should happen: Preferred addresses and indexing instructions match which pages should appear in search.

What to check: Use a narrow screen and larger text
What should happen: Important text and controls remain readable.
Content appears in a useful order without disruptive jumps.
You can reach and operate the important controls with visible focus.
Labels make sense, useful images have descriptions and reduced motion works.
An error explains what to fix without losing the valid details.

What to check: Send yourself a labeled test message
What should happen: On your own site, check confirmation, any saved record, inbox or spam, and your reply separately.
You know who controls the domain, hosting and tools; do not put passwords in this sheet.
Your web person can explain a saved version and a safe way to restore it.

What to check: Check the evidence for a change
What should happen: Use actual page, search or inquiry records with dates; unknown is not zero.

What to check: Repeat a failed task after a fix
What should happen: Record whether it now works; keep business results separate from a completed repair.
